newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey, Bulgaria work on common problems - Demirel.
newsitem.headline: Turkey, Bulgaria work on common problems - Demirel.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel said on Monday Turkey would work with Balkan neighbour Bulgaria on solving common problems during a visit to Ankara by his Bulgarian counterpart.

"We will strive toward a solution to common problems between our two countries in an atmosphere of genuine friendship and neighbourliness," Demirel said as he welcomed Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov at the presidential palace.

Ties between Moslem Turkey and its smaller Orthodox Christian neighbour are weighed down by five centuries of Ottoman rule in Bulgaria and the forcible assimilation of Bulgarian ethnic Turks in the last years of Communism.

Stoyanov is on a three-day trip to Turkey hoping improved ties can win the lifting of an Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) rating of Bulgaria as a country which does not respect Moslem rights.
"I will ask President Demirel to press for an OIC contact group to prepare a report on Moslems in Bulgaria ahead of December's OIC conference in Kuwait," Stoyanov said before departing Sofia.
Under OIC statutes, it is Turkey which must initiate Bulgaria's removal from the list as it was Turkey which sought its inclusion in 1989.

In 1989 the administration of former Communist dictator Todor Zhivkov ordered more than one million ethnic Turks to give up their Islamic names and religious traditions, leading to an exodus of more than 300,000 to Turkey and the OIC blacklisting.
Moslem religious and cultural rights were restored after Zhivkov's overthrow in November 1989 and many of those who left have returned.
Zhivkov is under house arrest while the ethnic Turks' Movement for Rights and Freedoms forms the third force in parliament.
